newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela rebuffs U.S. threat to cut aid over arms.
newsitem.headline: Mandela rebuffs U.S. threat to cut aid over arms.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Wednesday rejected a warning from the United States over a proposed arms deal with Syria, and said that South Africa would conclude deals with whichever country it chose.
"We will conclude agreements with any country whether they are popular in the West or not. And that is what we are likely to do in this case," Mandela told reporters at his Johannesburg home.

The United States said on Monday it was extremely concerned by news of South Africa's proposed sale to Syria of aim-enhancing gear worth $641 million for its Soviet-made tanks, and threatened to cut off aid if the deal went ahead.

"We will never allow any support or assistance from any country, no matter how powerful it is, to dictate our foreign policy, nor allow any country to violate our sovereignty and undermine our national pride," Mandela said.

In what was widely seen on Tuesday as a bid to back away from the arms deal, due to be discussed by cabinet on January 22, the Foreign Ministry said no contract had been signed and any deal for what it termed "software" was not likely to be concluded before 1999.
Mandela however said the statement did not imply any kind of backtracking under pressure from Washington.
"There is no question of backing down. They only say (in the ministry statement) that there has been no decision," he said.
U.S. aid to South Africa totals $120 million for 1997.
Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana reacted to the threat to cut U.S. aid by accusing Washington of high-handed bullying, telling Reuters on Tuesday:
"We detest this kind of behaviour...We just don't like being shouted at...We'd rather be spoken to differently, as equals, instead of (Washington) making public threats.
The United States has since adopted a softer line, saying that it will not make a decision on possibly reducing aid to South Africa until it gets more facts on the reported sale.
